experiment: Exp 37 — depth vs training-tokens confound RESOLVED (Pythia scale sweep)

preregistered.D1: if DEPTH drives collapse, pythia-70m (6L) and 160m (12L) keep variance like GPT-2 124M (12L)
preregistered.D2: if TRAINING EXPOSURE drives it, even 70m is collapsed AND 160m (same 12L depth as GPT-2 124M) is collapsed where GPT-2 is not

verdict: D2 CONFIRMED — the 'law of depth' was a confound: the driver is TRAINING EXPOSURE, not depth. Pythia-160m (12 layers, ~84B tokens of The Pile) is fully collapsed at square point while GPT-2 124M (12 layers, ~10B tokens of WebText) retains variance. Same architecture depth, different training scale, different collapse regime.
implications: 1) The collapse is a FUNCTION OF LEARNING: more tokens seen -> keys converge to the corpus's intrinsic redundancy. 2) The spectral criterion's operating range is determined by training exposure, measurable a priori. 3) RENAME: 'law of depth' -> 'law of training exposure'. 4) Prediction for deployment-scale models (7B+, trillions of tokens): fully collapsed everywhere; only sub-square measurement retains signal.
honest_label: Pythia-70m trained on The Pile (~84B tokens); GPT-2 124M on WebText (~10B effective). The confound 'depth vs tokens' is resolved by the 12L-vs-12L natural experiment, but corpus differences (Pile vs WebText) remain a secondary confound — the Pile is more diverse, which could contribute. A replication with pythia checkpoints (step 0 vs final) would fully isolate the token-count variable.
